title: Generative AI for Business: Complete Guide
summary: Learn how businesses are using generative AI to scale marketing, support, web design, and operations.
body_markdown:
Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has many applications for ecommerce businesses. It uses patterns learned from existing data to generate new content, such as product descriptions, customer support responses, sales summaries, and ad variations.


Adoption of generative AI technology is growing quickly, but adoption doesn’t guarantee results. According to[2025 S&P Global research](https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2025/10/generative-ai-shows-rapid-growth-but-yields-mixed-results) , 60% of organizations investing in AI had implemented generative AI, yet its impact varied. The report found that organizations were getting value from specific applications such as content creation, information summarization, process automation, and customer interaction.


For ecommerce businesses, getting value from generative AI starts with identifying the tasks where it can save time or help teams do more. This guide explores how business owners are using the technology across marketing, design, customer support, and operations, and how you can put these use cases into practice.


## What is generative AI for business?


[Generative AI](https://www.shopify.com/blog/generative-ai) is a type of machine learning that identifies patterns in large datasets and uses those patterns to create text, images, video, audio, and software code, among other new content.


This differs from other types of[machine learning](https://www.shopify.com/blog/machine-learning-in-ecommerce) and automation. Discriminative machine learning models, for example, identify patterns in existing data to make predictions or classifications, such as estimating how many units of a product you’ll sell next month. Rule-based automations, by contrast, follow predefined instructions, such as sending an email when a customer abandons a cart.


Generative AI models can work directly with unstructured data such as natural-language text. You can paste customer reviews or support transcripts into generative AI tools, for example, and ask them to summarize, categorize, or rewrite that information. You can also[connect a tool like ChatGPT or Claude](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/ai-powered-tools/connecting-ai-tools) directly to your Shopify store so it can access relevant store data without you copying it over.


Generative AI solutions can provide a starting point for tasks like drafting or summarizing content, but you bring your own expertise to the result. Always review AI-generated outputs based on your knowledge of your products, customers, and brand voice, and refine them as needed.

## Applying generative AI: Use cases


- Marketing copy
- Ad variations
- Design and storefront changes
- Customer support
- Operations and back office


Here’s how store owners are putting generative AI capabilities to work across different business functions:


### Marketing copy


Marketing copy is one way ecommerce businesses can use generative AI systems. AI models need context to generate copy that’s aligned with your brand and goals, so provide examples of your top-performing emails, product pages, or ads as additional training data.


Muammar Reed, cofounder of multicultural and multilingual bookseller[MiJa Books](https://mijabooks.com/) , uses generative AI to[repurpose original video content](https://www.shopify.com/blog/repurpose-content) into written assets. As he explains on *[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/mija-books-rewriting-the-business-of-books)* , he extracts captions from his videos, feeds the text into tools like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini, and asks the AI to turn the material into newsletters and social posts.


### Ad variations


Generative AI can help you create more ad variations to test, including different headlines, copy, images, and other creative elements.


Andrew Faris, founder of the growth agency[AJF Growth](https://ajfgrowth.com/) , uses a Claude project containing past ad scripts to help create new variations. Rather than asking AI to write an ad from scratch, Andrew writes a two- to three-minute video ad explainer script, asks Claude to cut it by 50%, and then asks it to cut the shortened version again. This yields long, medium, and short versions that he tests on Facebook, he says on *[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/andrew-faris-pnl)* .


[Ridge](https://ridge.com/) takes this approach further by automating ad creation at scale. The accessories brand uses a custom GPT loaded with examples of its best-performing ads and connects it to the automation tool n8n to generate about 500 static ads a day. CEO Sean Frank says on *[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ridge-wallets-using-ai-to-grow-revenue)* that roughly 90% aren’t good enough to run, but the remaining 10% provide additional creative the company can test. “It comes down to volume,” he says. “The future of advertising is just shots on goal.”


### Design and storefront changes


Generative AI tools can help you make storefront changes without manually editing code. In Shopify’s theme editor, for example, you can ask[Sidekick](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/sidekick/index) , the AI assistant built into the Shopify admin, in everyday language to adjust existing theme settings such as colors, typography, and spacing.[Shopify Magic](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/ai-powered-tools/shopify-magic) can also generate new theme blocks based on a description of what you want.


This can make it easier to experiment with temporary or seasonal designs. “You can redesign your site for Valentine’s Day and then the next day revert it,” says Alex Pilon, a Shopify developer and AI advocate, in an[interview with Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/blog/the-future-of-artificial-intelligence) . “It costs you a couple dollars of tokens instead of a thousand-dollar design agency fee.”


AI-generated storefront elements still require human review.[Shopify recommends](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/themes/customizing-themes/theme-editor/shopify-magic/generate-blocks) previewing and testing generated theme blocks on desktop and mobile before adding them to your store because generated code can contain errors or fail to meet best practices.


### Customer support


Generative AI can also help with[customer service](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ai-customer-service) by generating responses to customer questions. AI support tools can use information such as order details and store policies to help answer routine inquiries.[Shopify Inbox](https://inbox.shopify.com/) , the free chat app in your admin, uses Shopify Magic to suggest replies to live chat messages and answer common questions automatically. It also shows you what a shopper has in their cart while you talk to them. If you need more features—like support across email, social media, and SMS in one place—help desk apps like[Gorgias](https://apps.shopify.com/helpdesk) and[Richpanel](https://apps.shopify.com/customer-support) connect to your Shopify store and can help draft replies inside your support inbox.


At Ridge, AI now answers about 60% of customer support tickets, according to Sean. He says the company’s customer ratings have remained high as it has increased its use of AI for support. “It’s faster, it’s quicker, it’s more accurate,” he says.


### Operations and back office


Generative AI can help with back-office business processes like analyzing reports and drafting internal documents. For example, you can provide a tool with sales data and ask it to summarize trends or explain what the numbers show. You can also provide notes or key points and ask it to organize them into a draft.


At Ridge, Sean says his team pulls reports from Shopify and uses[ChatGPT](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ai-chatgpt) to help analyze them. Employees who previously manually compared data and crunched numbers can take screenshots of reports and drop them into ChatGPT for analysis. “Now my entire team is operating like data scientists,” Sean says.


Lindsey Carter, founder of the activewear brand[SET Active](https://setactive.co/) , used ChatGPT to draft feedback for a new assistant. She provided the issues she wanted to address and asked ChatGPT to help prioritize the tasks and organize the feedback into an email. “It took me five minutes,” she says on an episode of[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/set-active-inventory-management) . “Five years ago, that email probably would’ve taken me five hours to write out.”


## How to get started with generative AI for business


As generative AI adoption grows among small businesses, Alex’s advice for beginners is to skip an elaborate setup. “Interact with it as a thought partner,” he says. You can start with a general-purpose chat tool such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini and experiment with specific business challenges relevant to your work.


Once you have a feel for how generative AI performs, you can begin integrating generative AI into your existing workflows.[Connect supported AI tools](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/ai-powered-tools/connecting-ai-tools) to your Shopify admin and use relevant store data as context without manually copying or exporting it.


Knowing which tasks to give AI—and which still require your judgment—is a skill you can develop with experience. “AI is a great tool, and building instincts for what it’s good at and where you still add immeasurable value is top of mind for me,” Alex says.


Jaz Fenton, cofounder of design agency[Otherhalf Studio](https://otherhalf.studio/) , says on *[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/otherhalf-studio-designing-successfully)* that unless you[prompt AI](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ai-prompts) carefully, “it kind of does spit out pretty generic things.” She says human expertise remains important when you incorporate generative AI into creative workflows but still want to produce distinctive work.


## Generative AI for business FAQ


### How is generative AI used in businesses?


Common generative AI applications in ecommerce include writing[product descriptions](https://www.shopify.com/blog/8211159-9-simple-ways-to-write-product-descriptions-that-sell) and marketing copy, generating ad variations, drafting customer support replies and internal communications, and summarizing sales data.


### How do you use AI technology in a small business?


When adopting generative AI in a small business, start with a low-stakes task where you can review model outputs, such as drafting a product description, marketing email, or reply to a common customer question. Provide relevant context and examples, and then review the results for accuracy and make changes based on your knowledge of your products, customers, and brand.


### How much does business AI cost?


General-purpose tools like ChatGPT and Claude have limited free plans, with paid tiers ranging from $7 to $120 per month and $17 to $100 or more per month, respectively. The two LLMs also have a business offering for teams, starting at $20 per month per seat when billed annually. AI-powered tools, including Sidekick and Shopify Magic, are included with Shopify plans at no extra charge.
